rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 06/12/2025] An I.A.No.III filed by the Jdr is dismissed. The Memo filed by the Dhr is hereby allowed and E.P is closed as fully satisfied.
rows.Order Procedural History: The learned counsel for the Dhr filed memo stating that, the Dhr has taken possession of the suit property through court process. EP is fully satisfied. Hence, E.P may be closed. 2. The learned counsel for the Jdr filed I.A.No.II Under order 21 Rule 58 r/w. 151 of CPC and U/s.6 of Specific Relief Act seeking for restoration of his possession over suit property and further stated that he has legally disposed from the suit property. 3. Heard both sides. 4. The following points that arise for my consideration: :- Whether there is sufficient grounds for allow the I.A.No.III.? :-What Order ? 5. By considering the memo and I.A, and hearing of the parties, my answer for the above point is as under: :- In the Negative, :- As per final order 2
rows.Order Judicial Findings: for the following:- 7. :- The learned Dhr submitted that in order to cause delay the present application is filed by the Jdr. The Jdr is very well aware about the pending of this E.P. He ha kept quite until completion of the process of execution of the warrant, at the fag end of the case, he has filed false application. Hence, prays to reject the application. 8. The learned counsel for the Jdr submitted that after Jdr challenged the Judgment and order passed by this court in before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA.No.410/2023, the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka issued notice to Dhr. The Dhr has also appeared before the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in the said appeal. The Dhr has failed to comply the provision of order 21 Rule 34 (2) of CPC. He has not produced any E.C while executing of the sale deed. The Jdr has prima-facie case. Hence, 3 prays to allow the application and stay the proceedings and handover the possession in favour of the Jdr. 9. I have carefully perused the entire material on record. The Dhr has filed this Execution petition on 02.03.2023 and issued notice to the Jdr through paper publication. Notice to Jdr is served. In spite of that he has failed to appear before this court. Sale deed executed in favour of the Dhr through process. Thereafter, issued possession deliver warrant which was duly executed. In this case the Court Ameen has submitted his report, mahazar and possession receipt. The very object of the execution petition is already served. 10. Jdr not submitted regarding whether the execution of the Judgment and order passed by this court in is stayed by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka in RFA.No. 410/2023. By 4 considering all these aspects, I am of the opinion, present application is filed to defeat the very object of the speedy disposal of the case and to deny, obstruct the fruits of the decree. Therefore, I am of the opinion that there is no grounds to allow the I.A.No.III. Hence, point No.1 is answered in the Negative. 11. P oint No.3 :- In view of my findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following:
rows.Order Annexed Proceedings: 2. This order or compromise shall not binding on Robin paul who is plaintiff No.2 in . 3. This order and compromise shall not effect on merits of the suit . 4. this order and compromise shall not effect on protection of plaintiff No.1 in as pro- tected by granting temporary injunction in the said suit. (Sri. I. P. Naik) LXIII ACCL & SJ (CCH-64), BENGALURU CITY. 8

rows.Business Text: Case called out. Adv for DHR filed IA.No.III and IV U/s 151 of CPC, seeking for police protection at the time of execution of warrant and break open the door lock. Heard. Perused the IA.III and IV and report submitted by court Ameen. A court Ameen has expressed his apprehension of disturb from the JDR while executing the warrant. Therefore he need police help. By considering all these aspects, it is necessary to provide police protection to court Ameen while executing the possession delivery warrant and also removing of lock. Accordingly both IA’s are allowed. The jurisdictional police is hereby directed to provide necessary protection to court Ameen while executing posession delivery warrant. A court Ameen is at liberty to break open the lock installed to suit property if it is locked. Office is directed to issue intimation to jurisdictional police to provide protection to court Ameen. Issue possession delivery warrant if PF paid returnable by 25.11.2025.

rows.Business Text: Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR filed IA.No.II U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC, seeking for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose perform ministerial act of this court. Heard. The learned counel for DHR urged that, in this case this court granted relief of specific performance of contract by passing judgment and decree in O.S.No.4555/2020 dated 02.07.2022. As per the said judgment and decree the JDR is requires to execute sale deed in favour of DHR petitioner within 3 months from the date judgment. The JDR fails to execute sale deed by receiving remaining balance sale consideration. Hence, prays for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose of execution of sale deed on behalf of JDR. I have perused the IA.No.I, petition and decree. In O.S.No.4555/2020 this court decreed the suit of the plaintiff and directed to defendant execute the sale deed by receiving sale consideration within 3 months from 02.07.2022. There is no record to show that, the judgement passed by this court is setaside or stayed by competant court of law. It is just and proper to appointment of court commissioner for performing minsterial act on behalf of this court. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER IA.No.II filed U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC is hereby consider as filed U/o 26 rule 10-B of CPC and hereby allowed. One Advocate of Advocate’s Bar Bengaluru is appointed as court commissioner. The learned counsel for DHR filed memo with draft sale deed. Call on by 08.08.2024.

hearings.business_text: Case called out. Learned counsel for DHR filed IA.No.II U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC, seeking for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose perform ministerial act of this court. Heard. The learned counel for DHR urged that, in this case this court granted relief of specific performance of contract by passing judgment and decree in O.S.No.4555/2020 dated 02.07.2022. As per the said judgment and decree the JDR is requires to execute sale deed in favour of DHR petitioner within 3 months from the date judgment. The JDR fails to execute sale deed by receiving remaining balance sale consideration. Hence, prays for appointment of court commissioner for the purpose of execution of sale deed on behalf of JDR. I have perused the IA.No.I, petition and decree. In O.S.No.4555/2020 this court decreed the suit of the plaintiff and directed to defendant execute the sale deed by receiving sale consideration within 3 months from 02.07.2022. There is no record to show that, the judgement passed by this court is setaside or stayed by competant court of law. It is just and proper to appointment of court commissioner for performing minsterial act on behalf of this court. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:- ORDER IA.No.II filed U/o 26 rule 9 of CPC is hereby consider as filed U/o 26 rule 10-B of CPC and hereby allowed. One Advocate of Advocate’s Bar Bengaluru is appointed as court commissioner. The learned counsel for DHR filed memo with draft sale deed. Call on by 08.08.2024.

rows.Case Title: H L L LIFECARE LIMITED vs M/S SUPER THREADS INDIA
rows.Court Name: PRL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Court Room & Judge: 18-CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 30/09/2024] 10 Ex.P.No.16/2023 District Court Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, on an application filed u/Sec.11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act appointed an arbitrator. The Hon'ble High Court of Trivandrum is having jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondents in the year 2017 filed I.A. u/Sec.11 of the Act stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order that an arbitrator be appointed. Inspite of issuance of reply, the decree holder has failed to furnish required documents i.e. entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The learned counsel for the judgment debtor has relied upon rulings reported in:- (1) 2019 SCCOnline KAR 276 (Para No.8 and 9), in the case of Mohammed Shafi and another V/s. Mohammed Ashapak Hussain. (2) 1972 (2) SCC 662 (Headnote B; Para 3) in the case of Sunder Dass V/s. Ram Prakash.
rows.Order Procedural History: 6 Ex.P.No.16/2023 ORDERS The learned counsel for JDR has filed preliminary objections contending that this Court has no any jurisdiction to entertain this petition as the District Court in Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, passed an order on an application filed u/Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. For brevity (here in after referred to as Act) and appointed an arbitrator. As per Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, application can be filed only before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka. The application is not maintainable before a District Judge. In view of the same, the arbitrator appointed has lacked inherent jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties and pass any award. Hence, the award passed by the arbitrator is a nullity in law and there can be no enforcement of any award passed by the arbitrator in the present case. Any enforcement of this award that is patently illegal would be against public order and justice. The decree holder had fraudulently approached the Hukkeri District Court and filed in spite of being aware that 7 Ex.P.No.16/2023 the respondent was present in Bengaluru and no cause of action has arisen in Hukkeri District. As per arbitration clause, the Courts of Trivandrum had jurisdiction of power, authority to adjudicate any disputes between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondent has filed I.A. under Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in the year 2017 stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order an arbitrator be appointed. As per Sec.11 of the Act, the application could be maintainable only in the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala. Hence, the District Court in without application of mind and without any jurisdiction appointed an arbitrator by name Sri.Ashok B. Bolgundi who is a practicing advocate in Belgaum district. At first instance when the arbitrator issued the notice to appear the judgment debtor brought it to the arbitrator's notice that he had no jurisdiction to adjudicate the disputes between the parties. However, the arbitrator was hands in glove with the decree holder and the award was illegally passed. In fact there were no
rows.Order Judicial Findings: 8 Ex.P.No.16/2023 correspondences between the parties and the arbitrator after the issue of jurisdiction was raised and the judgment debtor safely presumed that the arbitration ceased to exit. However, the Decree Holder issued a notice dated 02.02.2018 that an award was passed and called upon the judgment debtor to pay money. The judgment debtor has issued reply on 15.02.2018 requesting the decree holder to send the entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also the entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The decree holder undertook to pay the entire cost for the same. The judgment debtor once again issued a notice on 29.08.2018 requesting the decree holder to send the required document immediately. There was complete silence for 6 years and by suppressing materials and by playing fraud, the decree holder has filed this execution petition to extort money from the judgment debtor. The decree holder with malafide intention to harass the judgment debtor fraudulently obtained an illegal award and has filed this execution petition. The decree holder is a public sector undertaking 9 Ex.P.No.16/2023 and owing to the afore mentioned reasons the execution petition be dismissed by imposing heavy costs. Heard the arguments of learned respective counsels, reply arguments of learned counsel for JDR. Perused materials available on record. The points that arise for consideration and determination are as under:- 1. Whether this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain this petition? 2. What order? This Court answer above points as under:- : In Negative, : As per the final order for the following:- :- It is the case of the JDR that this Court has no jurisdiction as the 10 Ex.P.No.16/2023 District Court Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, on an application filed u/Sec.11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act appointed an arbitrator. The Hon'ble High Court of Trivandrum is having jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondents in the year 2017 filed I.A. u/Sec.11 of the Act stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order that an arbitrator be appointed. Inspite of issuance of reply, the decree holder has failed to furnish required documents i.e. entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The learned counsel for the judgment debtor has relied upon rulings reported in:- (1) 2019 SCCOnline KAR 276 (Para No.8 and 9), in the case of Mohammed Shafi and another V/s. Mohammed Ashapak Hussain. (2) 1972 (2) SCC 662 (Headnote B; Para 3) in the case of Sunder Dass V/s. Ram Prakash.
rows.Order Annexed Proceedings: 13 Ex.P.No.16/2023 the decree where the decree sought to be executed is a nullity for lack of inherent jurisdiction and its invalidity can be set up in execution proceeding is not applicable to the present case in hand looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of case. The JDR should have been vigilant enough when he has filed application to set aside / windup arbitration proceedings in the year 2017 i.e. 25.02.2017. This Court is of considered opinion that this Court has jurisdiction to entertain and to decide the petition. Hence, preliminary objection raised by the JDR is not applicable to the present case in hand. Accordingly, the say of the JDR that this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain this petition is negated. XVII Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.
rows.Hearing Judge: CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Business Text: Case advanced. Counsel for Jdr placed before the copy of the order passed by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in W.P No.33607/2024 dated 26-09-2025, whereby the Hon'ble High Court quashed the order dated 05-12-2024 passed by this court in present Ex.P No.16/2023 and consequently declared that award passed by the Arbitrator is invalid and unenforcible. Further ordered that the original suit filed by the respondent i.e. the Dhr herein on the file of Senior Civil Judge, Hukkeri is restored and in order to expediate the suit, the petitioner as well as respondent are directed to appear before the Trial Court on 13-10-2025 and it is open for the petitioner and respondent to seek appointment of an Arbitrator in accordance with law and as provided u/s 11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. In view of afore mentioned order of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka the present execution petition which is filed for enforcement of the award passed by the Arbitrator, pursuant to his appointment by the court of Senior Civil Judge, Hukkeri needs to be closed. Accordingly, petition is hereby closed.

rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 30/09/2024] 10 Ex.P.No.16/2023 District Court Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, on an application filed u/Sec.11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act appointed an arbitrator. The Hon'ble High Court of Trivandrum is having jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondents in the year 2017 filed I.A. u/Sec.11 of the Act stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order that an arbitrator be appointed. Inspite of issuance of reply, the decree holder has failed to furnish required documents i.e. entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The learned counsel for the judgment debtor has relied upon rulings reported in:- (1) 2019 SCCOnline KAR 276 (Para No.8 and 9), in the case of Mohammed Shafi and another V/s. Mohammed Ashapak Hussain. (2) 1972 (2) SCC 662 (Headnote B; Para 3) in the case of Sunder Dass V/s. Ram Prakash.
rows.Order Procedural History: 6 Ex.P.No.16/2023 ORDERS The learned counsel for JDR has filed preliminary objections contending that this Court has no any jurisdiction to entertain this petition as the District Court in Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, passed an order on an application filed u/Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. For brevity (here in after referred to as Act) and appointed an arbitrator. As per Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, application can be filed only before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka. The application is not maintainable before a District Judge. In view of the same, the arbitrator appointed has lacked inherent jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties and pass any award. Hence, the award passed by the arbitrator is a nullity in law and there can be no enforcement of any award passed by the arbitrator in the present case. Any enforcement of this award that is patently illegal would be against public order and justice. The decree holder had fraudulently approached the Hukkeri District Court and filed in spite of being aware that 7 Ex.P.No.16/2023 the respondent was present in Bengaluru and no cause of action has arisen in Hukkeri District. As per arbitration clause, the Courts of Trivandrum had jurisdiction of power, authority to adjudicate any disputes between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondent has filed I.A. under Sec.11 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in the year 2017 stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order an arbitrator be appointed. As per Sec.11 of the Act, the application could be maintainable only in the Hon'ble High Court of Kerala. Hence, the District Court in without application of mind and without any jurisdiction appointed an arbitrator by name Sri.Ashok B. Bolgundi who is a practicing advocate in Belgaum district. At first instance when the arbitrator issued the notice to appear the judgment debtor brought it to the arbitrator's notice that he had no jurisdiction to adjudicate the disputes between the parties. However, the arbitrator was hands in glove with the decree holder and the award was illegally passed. In fact there were no
rows.Order Judicial Findings: 8 Ex.P.No.16/2023 correspondences between the parties and the arbitrator after the issue of jurisdiction was raised and the judgment debtor safely presumed that the arbitration ceased to exit. However, the Decree Holder issued a notice dated 02.02.2018 that an award was passed and called upon the judgment debtor to pay money. The judgment debtor has issued reply on 15.02.2018 requesting the decree holder to send the entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also the entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The decree holder undertook to pay the entire cost for the same. The judgment debtor once again issued a notice on 29.08.2018 requesting the decree holder to send the required document immediately. There was complete silence for 6 years and by suppressing materials and by playing fraud, the decree holder has filed this execution petition to extort money from the judgment debtor. The decree holder with malafide intention to harass the judgment debtor fraudulently obtained an illegal award and has filed this execution petition. The decree holder is a public sector undertaking 9 Ex.P.No.16/2023 and owing to the afore mentioned reasons the execution petition be dismissed by imposing heavy costs. Heard the arguments of learned respective counsels, reply arguments of learned counsel for JDR. Perused materials available on record. The points that arise for consideration and determination are as under:- 1. Whether this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain this petition? 2. What order? This Court answer above points as under:- : In Negative, : As per the final order for the following:- :- It is the case of the JDR that this Court has no jurisdiction as the 10 Ex.P.No.16/2023 District Court Hukkeri without having any jurisdiction, on an application filed u/Sec.11 of Arbitration and Conciliation Act appointed an arbitrator. The Hon'ble High Court of Trivandrum is having jurisdiction to adjudicate any dispute between the parties after two years of filing the suit bearing . The respondents in the year 2017 filed I.A. u/Sec.11 of the Act stating that since there is an arbitration clause in the purchase order that an arbitrator be appointed. Inspite of issuance of reply, the decree holder has failed to furnish required documents i.e. entire order sheet, judgment, decree in and also entire order sheet maintained by the arbitrator. The learned counsel for the judgment debtor has relied upon rulings reported in:- (1) 2019 SCCOnline KAR 276 (Para No.8 and 9), in the case of Mohammed Shafi and another V/s. Mohammed Ashapak Hussain. (2) 1972 (2) SCC 662 (Headnote B; Para 3) in the case of Sunder Dass V/s. Ram Prakash.
rows.Order Annexed Proceedings: 13 Ex.P.No.16/2023 the decree where the decree sought to be executed is a nullity for lack of inherent jurisdiction and its invalidity can be set up in execution proceeding is not applicable to the present case in hand looking to the peculiar facts and circumstances of case. The JDR should have been vigilant enough when he has filed application to set aside / windup arbitration proceedings in the year 2017 i.e. 25.02.2017. This Court is of considered opinion that this Court has jurisdiction to entertain and to decide the petition. Hence, preliminary objection raised by the JDR is not applicable to the present case in hand. Accordingly, the say of the JDR that this Court has no jurisdiction to entertain this petition is negated. XVII Addl. City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru.
rows.Hearing Judge: CCH16 XVII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE

hearings.business_text: Decree holder absent. No representation. Call on 03.00 PM/ (Sign) Case again called out at 04.00 PM. Decree holder absent. No representation. On perusal of order sheet it is found that inspite availing sufficient opportunities the Decree holder has continuously remained absent before the court and has not come forward to take steps for further proceedings of the matter. Hence, in view of the continuous absent of Decree holder from 06.03.2024, 26.04.2024,, 13.06.2024, 26.07.2024, 18.10.2024/19.10.2024, 22.11.2024 and today i.e., 19.12.2024 it appears that the Decree holder is not interested in proceeding in further in the matter. Hence, in view of continuous absence. The Decree holder and their Counsel are non taking of steps the execution petition is dismissed for default.

rows.Business Text: Show cause notice to the Spl. Thasildhar has been duly served, under which this court had sought the explanation to the salary drawing officer of the JDR herein for not attaching the salary of the JDR to satisfy the decree. The service of the show cause notice to the garnishee of the JDR has been reported to this court. Thus Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk has fails to send his explanation and fails to appear before this court, thus this court felt, it is proper to call the Spl. Thasildhar to be present before this court. Accordingly ordered to issue notice to the Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk Yelahanka, Bangalore to place his physicall appearance before this court on next date of hearing without fail. In this case, despite issuance of S/A/W to the garnishee of the JDR the same has not been carried out by the garnishee and despite service of show cause notice the garnishee remained absent. If that aspect is considered the garnishee may be hand in glow of the JDR, with intend to frustrate the decree of this court. Thus this court felt it is proper to order for issue arrest notice to the JDR. Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on IA.No. 2. As the DHR made out the grounds that it is the JDR and his garnishee with intend to frustrate the decree are evading the process of this court, thus IA.No. 2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed, ordered to issue arrest notice against the JDR, if the DHR pays the PF in the office. Call on 07.12.2023

As the DHR is filed the application to recover the petition amount by attaching the salary of the JDR herein, thus the objection raised by the office on not furnishing the list of movables is hereby overruled. hearings.business_text: Show cause notice to the Spl. Thasildhar has been duly served, under which this court had sought the explanation to the salary drawing officer of the JDR herein for not attaching the salary of the JDR to satisfy the decree. The service of the show cause notice to the garnishee of the JDR has been reported to this court. Thus Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk has fails to send his explanation and fails to appear before this court, thus this court felt, it is proper to call the Spl. Thasildhar to be present before this court. Accordingly ordered to issue notice to the Spl. Thasildhar Yelahanka Taluk Yelahanka, Bangalore to place his physicall appearance before this court on next date of hearing without fail. In this case, despite issuance of S/A/W to the garnishee of the JDR the same has not been carried out by the garnishee and despite service of show cause notice the garnishee remained absent. If that aspect is considered the garnishee may be hand in glow of the JDR, with intend to frustrate the decree of this court. Thus this court felt it is proper to order for issue arrest notice to the JDR. Heard the arguments of the L/c for the DHR on IA.No. 2. As the DHR made out the grounds that it is the JDR and his garnishee with intend to frustrate the decree are evading the process of this court, thus IA.No. 2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed, ordered to issue arrest notice against the JDR, if the DHR pays the PF in the office. Call on 07.12.2023

hearings.business_text: PF paid. As the DHR is filed the application to recover the petition amount by attaching the salary of the JDR herein, thus the objection raised by the office on not furnishing the list of movables is hereby overruled. DHR files IA.No.1 u/o 21 R 41 and 46 of CPC by seeking an order for attaching the salary of the JDR who works as peon in the office of the spl.Tasildhar Bangalore north taluk. As the execution petition is filed within 2 years, thus C/N to the JDR is dispensed and there is no office note to suggest that the preferring of appeal against the Judgment and decree and operation of any stay on the Judgment and decree of this court. Thus the DHR made out the grounds to allow IA.No.1 to attach the salary of the JDR to recover the petition amount. Accordingly IA.No.1 is hereby allowed, Issue Salary attachment warrant to the Spl.Tasildhar Bangalore north taluk, Yelahanka Bangalore city 560064 to attach petition amount. Call on 27.03.2023

Re-issue delivery warrant with a permission to break open the lock. Await report by 2.9.2023.

rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 08/07/2023] EX 102/2023 D.Hr and J.Dr and their respective counsels are present. Both parties have agreed the settlement and the dispute, the D.Hr and J.Dr had settled the dispute in Crl.A. No.1077/2021 for a sum of Rs.4,10,000/- and had paid Rs.1,57,000/- and for the remaining amount the D.Hr had filed the execution petition for recovery of Rs.2,53,000/-, the J.Dr had paid an amount of Rs.2,17,600/- earlier. Now the the J.Dr paid an amount of Rs.35400/- as full and final settlement in the execution petition. The D.Hr and his counsel have accepted the settlement and have received an amount of Rs.35400/- in cash and have acknowledged the same and have joint memo accepting the settlement. Joint memo is taken on record. Execution petition is settled before National Lok Adalath as full and final settlement in the presence of conciliators on this 8th day of July 2023. Sd/- (HEMANTH KUMAR C.R) Judicial / Conciliator Sd/- (B.C. Chaluvaraju) Advocate / Conciliator

rows.Process Title: Notice to show cause why execution should not issue [O. 21, R. 16]
rows.Hearing Judge: CCH66 LXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Business Text: D.Hr and J.Dr are present. D.Hr counsel and J.Dr counsel are present. J.Dr counsel files memo along with DD bearing No.183189, dt:15.02.2023 for Rs.45,000/- drawn on Karnataka Bank ltd., same is acknowledged by D.Hr. The present execution petition is filed to execute the joint memo filed in Crl.A No.1077/2021 before the lok adalath. The said Crl.A. No.1077/2021 was disposed in terms of joint memo on 25.06.2022. The Appellant having not complied with the terms of joint memo the present execution is filed. The said case in Crl.A. No.1077/2021 has been disposed in terms of joint memo before the lok adalath on 25.06.2022 and in the said joint memo the Appellant was given the liberty to withdraw the 20% amount deposited in CC No.14317/2020 before 36th ACMM. Though the Appellant was given the liberty to withdraw the amount and to pay the same to Respondent. The Appellant has not withdrawn the said 20% amount and has not paid to the Respondent as per joint memo dated 25.06.2022. Now both the Appellant and Respondent in Crl.A. No.1077/2021 are present and the Appellant in the said appeal No.1077/2021 has agreed and has stated that the he has no objection to the Respondent to withdraw the 20% of deposited amount which he has deposited before the trial court. The Appellant submits no objection to the Respondent to withdraw his amount of 20% deposited in CC. No.14317/2020 in terms of joint memo. The trial court is directed to release the 20% deposited amount in CC No.14317/2020 to the complainant R.Madhusudan Reddy on proper verification. J.Dr counsel prays time to pay remaining balance amount, by 09.03.2023

rows.Business Text: Statement of objection have been filed by JDR advocate. As per statement of objection cheque bearing no. 230962 dated 29.03.2014 of Rs.1,84,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 215 of Bheemanakuppe Village has been numbered as LAC 57/2014 and the same day the JDR has sent another cheque bearing no.230963 dated 29.03.2014 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 205 of Bheemanakuppe Village, which was numbered as LAC 64/2014. It is stated that the office while registering the above cases with regard to amount in LAC 64/2014 have deposited the amount of Rs.1,84,00,000/- instead of Rs. 1,18,00,000/- and vice versa. The office while depositing the amount in LAC 57/2014 have deposited a sum of Rs.1,18,00,000/- instead of Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of both the records in LAC 57/2014 and 64/2014 it is seen that with regard to LAC 64/2014 the BDA has sent letter dated 09.04.2014 along with cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of record in LAC 57/2014 it is seen that BDA has sent letter No.885/09-10 cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/-. There is mistake committed by the office in taking the cheques in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014. Hence, the amount deposited in respect of cheque no.230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 57/2014 and the amount deposited in respect of cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 64/2014. Copy of this order to be entered in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014 . Call on 22-08-2023.

hearings.business_text: Statement of objection have been filed by JDR advocate. As per statement of objection cheque bearing no. 230962 dated 29.03.2014 of Rs.1,84,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 215 of Bheemanakuppe Village has been numbered as LAC 57/2014 and the same day the JDR has sent another cheque bearing no.230963 dated 29.03.2014 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- pertaining to survey no. 205 of Bheemanakuppe Village, which was numbered as LAC 64/2014. It is stated that the office while registering the above cases with regard to amount in LAC 64/2014 have deposited the amount of Rs.1,84,00,000/- instead of Rs. 1,18,00,000/- and vice versa. The office while depositing the amount in LAC 57/2014 have deposited a sum of Rs.1,18,00,000/- instead of Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of both the records in LAC 57/2014 and 64/2014 it is seen that with regard to LAC 64/2014 the BDA has sent letter dated 09.04.2014 along with cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/-. On perusal of record in LAC 57/2014 it is seen that BDA has sent letter No.885/09-10 cheque no. 230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- but the office has taken cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/-. There is mistake committed by the office in taking the cheques in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014. Hence, the amount deposited in respect of cheque no.230963 for Rs.1,84,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 57/2014 and the amount deposited in respect of cheque no. 230962 for Rs.1,18,00,000/- has to be transferred to LAC 64/2014. Copy of this order to be entered in LAC 57/2014 and LAC 64/2014 . Call on 22-08-2023.

rows.Order Procedural History: Case called out. Counsel for DHR twice called out, absent. Upon perusal of order sheet, it is noticed that, on the earlier dates of hearing, the counsel for DHR was directed to take steps against JDR No.1 and 2 for the issuance of cause notices. Despite providing multiple opportunities, the DHR has failed to take proper steps against Jdr No.1 for taking steps to issue cause notices in order to effectively execute the decree. In view of the judgment of Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in Periyammal (Dead) through LRs & Ors. Vs. V. Rajamani & Anr. in Civil Appeal Nos. 3640- 3642/2025, wherein the Apex Court, by order dated 06.03.2025 and in compliance of the circular No.2/2025 dated 01.04.2025 issued by the Hon’ble High Court of Karnataka mandating the disposal of execution petitions within 6 months, this Court is duty bound to prevent undue pendency of the execution petitions. Since the DHR has not diligently pursued the execution and no purpose would be served in keeping the petition pending further, the execution petition deserves to be disposed of. Accordingly, the execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. The decree-holder is at liberty to take appropriate steps in accordance with law. Office is directed to return the copy of decree to the counsel for DHR upon verification and identification. 22.08.2026 XXXIV ACC & SJ., & Spl. Judge, (NDPS), Bengaluru. (CCH-35)

The petition is taken up before National Lok-adalath. The decree holder and his counsel present and after conciliation, they filed a memo stating that, the matter is settled as the JDR has fully satisfied the decree and prays to close the execution petition in terms of the memo filed. Since, the parties have settled the matter, the salary warrant issued against JDRs No.2 to 5 is hereby recalled.

rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 22/01/2026] EX 128/2023 No representation from the side of the Decree Holder. On perusal of the order sheet it is clear that this execution petition has been filed in the year 2023 for the recovery of the money. However, from last 2 years the Dhr is not taking steps against the Jdr correctly. Even today Decree Holder is not ready in order to proceed with the case. Therefore, it is not proper to grant further time to the Decree Holder to take steps against Jdr. The prayer of the advocate for the Dhr is hereby rejected. The above execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. IX A.C.C. & S.J., Bengaluru.

judicial_order.operative_ruling: [Order Dated: 15/07/2026] EX 129/2023 Decree Holder absent. Advocate for Decree Holder is also absent. No representation from the side of the Decree Holder. On perusal of the entire order sheet it is clear that the above execution petition has been filed for the recovery of the money in the year 2023. However, from the date of filing of the execution petition till today the Dhr did not came before the court in order to take steps against the Jdr correctly. Therefore, it is not proper to grant further time to the Decree Holder in order to proceed with the case. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following : ORDER The execution petition is dismissed for non prosecution. IX A.C.C. & S.J., Bengaluru.

rows.Business Text: Counsel for Jdr filed I.A.No. 1 and 2 U/S 151 of CPC, and U/O 21 Rule 26 of CPC, seeking to dismiss the petition and stay the Execution. Dhr counsel submits he has no written objections and he orally objections to I.A.No. 2. Heard both counsels on I.A. No. 1 and 2, since the grounds in urged in I.A.No. 1 or the grounds for filing appeal and petition can not be dismissed on the grounds stated in I.A.No. 1 and Jdrs counsels has submitted that already Jdr has filed appeal, application U/O 21 Rule 26 is maintainable if it is filed before filing appeal only, hence already appeal is filed by the jdr if jdr wants to stay order he has to approach appellate court only, hence I.A.No. 1 and 2 are rejected. Issue A/W/M of Jdr. Call on 30-05-2023.

rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 13/07/2024] EX158/2023 Case called before lokadalath on 13.07.2024. The parties and their respective Counsels present and files Joint memo stating that on conciliation they have amicably settled the dispute between them with the following terms and conditions: The JDR has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.35,000/­ to the DHR by way of DD within one week from today, towards full and final settlement and the DHR has agreed the same. Perused the Joint memo and records. The memo bears the signature of the parties and their respective counsels. They also produced ID proof documents for the inspection. We are of the opinion that the petition has been adjusted by lawful agreement in writing and signed by the parties and the compromise is lawful and voluntary one. Hence, the memo is accepted and allowed. Execution petition is closed in terms of the joint memo. Judicial Conciliator Advocate Conciliator 13.07.2024 13.07.2024

rows.Order Operative Ruling: [Order Dated: 26/06/2023] 26-06-2023 Case advanced. Counsel for DHR filed application U/s.40 CPC seeking to transfer the Decree to Senior Civil Judge Court at Chitoor, Andhra Pradesh. In view of the above observations this Court is of the opinion that under these circumstances the Jdr No.1 would not get any prejudice or loss. Therefore this Court is hereby directing the Jdr No.2 to attach service benefits of the Jdr No.1 not exceeding Rs. 5,86,060/- and deposit the same by way of D.D. in favour of this court. By directing to Jdr No.2, issue attachment of the service benefits of Jdr No.1 not exceeding amount of Rs. 5,86,060/-. Call on 08-02-2023.

rows.Hearing Judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Business Text: PF paid. Reissue A/W/M against the JDR. DHR files IA.No. 2 U/s 151 of CPC to extend the police protections to the bailiff of this court to execute the A/W/M issued against the JDR on the ground that the JDR has obstructed for the execution of the A/W/M and also sought the break opening of the lock of the premises of the JDR\''s to attach his movables. The A/W/M issued by this court returned unexecuted with a report that the JDR has obstructed for the execution of A/w/M and thus he sought the police protection. By considering the same this court is of the opinion as the JDR is obstructing for the execution of warrant it is proper to order the Jurisdictional Rajgopalanagar PS to extend the police security to the bailiff of this court to execute the A/W/M issued against the JDR. And also ordered to the bailiff to break open the lock of the premises of the JDR if his premises is kept locked to prevent the execution of warrant when he visits to the JDR\''s place for execution. Office is to send intimation to the Jurisdictional Rajgopalanagar PS to extend the police security to the bailiff of this court to execute the A/W/M issued against the JDR. Call on 01.06.2023

rows.Business Text: The Delivery warrant issued against the JDR returned unexecuted as kept locked and also reported that the JDR has inducted the tenants in the petition schedule property. As the decree for possession, the tenants under the possession of the JDR are bound by the decree. Thus this court felt they are not necessary party before this court to issue notice to them. Considering the same, this court felt proper to re-issue Delivery warrant with directions to break open the lock of the petition schedule property. The DHR files IA.No.2 u/O 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to break open the locks of the petition schedule properties and to deliver the vacant possession in favor of the DHR herein. As the JDR is obstructing the executing the Delivery warrant by kept locking the petition schedule property and appears to be inducted some 3rd party into the petition schedule property to delay the execution proceedings. Thus IA.No.2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Ordered to issue Delivery warrant with directions to the bailiff to break open the lock of the petition schedule property and demolish the building stands on the petition schedule property with the assistance of the men and material of the DHR and deliver the vacant petition schedule property in favour of the DHR. Directed the DHR to extend with sufficient men and material to demolish the building found on the petition schedule property. And also directed the jurisdictional Hebbal police to extend the police protection to the officer of this court to execute the Delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favor of the DHR herein. Call on 09.11.2023.

rows.Business Text: Sri LB files vakalath for JDR and files IA.No. 1 u/o 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to issue delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the existed structure with the police protections. In this case, the DHR has got the decree for possession wherein, directed the JDR herein to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the building existed therein within 90 days from the date of Judgment. The Judgment dt 27.01.2022 and the JDR submitted the against the Judgment and decree of this cour the JDR has not preferred an appeal, thus this court felt as the JDR is fails to comply the Judgment and Decree, thus it is proper to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favour of DHR herein by executing the delivery warrant. Accordingly IA.No. 1 is hereby allowed, delivery warrant is been issued to deliver the petition schedule property in favour of the DHR herein and permitted the bailiff of this court to take sufficient assistance to demolish the building existed on petition schedule property. Thus directed the DHR to extend his all assistance by providing men and machinery to carryout the demolition work and liberty is being given to the DHR to file calculation memo on the expenditure made for the demolition to recover from the JDR. To avoid the obstruction if any to come in the way of bailiff to execute the warrant to deliver the possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the structure therein it is proper to extend police security. Thus directed the police inspector attached to the Jurisdiction Hebbal Police station to extend the police protections to the officer of this court to execute the warrant as and when he approaches the police station by providing sufficient men. For await report. Call on 30.08.2023

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: The Delivery warrant issued against the JDR returned unexecuted as kept locked and also reported that the JDR has inducted the tenants in the petition schedule property. As the decree for possession, the tenants under the possession of the JDR are bound by the decree. Thus this court felt they are not necessary party before this court to issue notice to them. Considering the same, this court felt proper to re-issue Delivery warrant with directions to break open the lock of the petition schedule property. The DHR files IA.No.2 u/O 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to break open the locks of the petition schedule properties and to deliver the vacant possession in favor of the DHR herein. As the JDR is obstructing the executing the Delivery warrant by kept locking the petition schedule property and appears to be inducted some 3rd party into the petition schedule property to delay the execution proceedings. Thus IA.No.2 filed by the DHR is hereby allowed. Ordered to issue Delivery warrant with directions to the bailiff to break open the lock of the petition schedule property and demolish the building stands on the petition schedule property with the assistance of the men and material of the DHR and deliver the vacant petition schedule property in favour of the DHR. Directed the DHR to extend with sufficient men and material to demolish the building found on the petition schedule property. And also directed the jurisdictional Hebbal police to extend the police protection to the officer of this court to execute the Delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favor of the DHR herein. Call on 09.11.2023.

hearings.judge: CCH27 XII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Sri LB files vakalath for JDR and files IA.No. 1 u/o 21 R 35 of CPC by seeking an order to issue delivery warrant to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the existed structure with the police protections. In this case, the DHR has got the decree for possession wherein, directed the JDR herein to deliver the vacant possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the building existed therein within 90 days from the date of Judgment. The Judgment dt 27.01.2022 and the JDR submitted the against the Judgment and decree of this cour the JDR has not preferred an appeal, thus this court felt as the JDR is fails to comply the Judgment and Decree, thus it is proper to deliver the vacant possession of the petition schedule property in favour of DHR herein by executing the delivery warrant. Accordingly IA.No. 1 is hereby allowed, delivery warrant is been issued to deliver the petition schedule property in favour of the DHR herein and permitted the bailiff of this court to take sufficient assistance to demolish the building existed on petition schedule property. Thus directed the DHR to extend his all assistance by providing men and machinery to carryout the demolition work and liberty is being given to the DHR to file calculation memo on the expenditure made for the demolition to recover from the JDR. To avoid the obstruction if any to come in the way of bailiff to execute the warrant to deliver the possession of petition schedule property by demolishing the structure therein it is proper to extend police security. Thus directed the police inspector attached to the Jurisdiction Hebbal Police station to extend the police protections to the officer of this court to execute the warrant as and when he approaches the police station by providing sufficient men. For await report. Call on 30.08.2023

rows.Order Procedural History: Ex.221/2023 Date: 16.03.2024 Case called before Lok Adalath. Decree Holder present. Learned counsel for Decree Holder present. Judgment Debtor absent. The learned counsel for the Judgment Debtor has submitted that he has been instructed to enter into compromise with the Decree Holder. In view of the same after conciliation and after the advise of the conciliators as well as learned counsels appearing for both the parties, the matter is settled for Rs.70,000/- to be paid by Judgment Debtor to the Decree Holder today itself. In view of the said compromise, the learned counsel for Judgment Debtor has paid Rs.70,000/- to the Decree Holder in cash. The Decree Holder reports and accepts the same before the Lok Adalath. In view of payment of Rs.70,000/- by the learned counsel for Judgment Debtor to Decree Holder the matter is settled and the Execution Petition stands closed as fully satisfied. Office is directed to draw award accordingly. Judicial Conciliator (K.S VIJAYA) Advocate conciliator (RUDRESH V.C)

rows.Hearing Judge: CCH67 LXVI ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Business Text: Passed over on submission of the counsel for DHR. Again called at 3-20 pm. The DHR counsel submits that I.A.No.3 is not pressing. Hence, I.A.No.3 is dismissed as not pressed. The DHR counsel is present. She filed I.A.No.4 under Order XXI Rule 43 of CPC for attachment of movable property as per the inventory made by the bailiff and I.A.No.5 under Order XXI Rule 64 of CPC for sale of movable properties by public action. Heard the counsel for DHR on I.A.No.4 and 5. Perused the record. The DHR has filed EP for execution of decree in OS.No.2524/2022 for delivery warrant and also for recovery of arrears of rent. As per the report of bailiff dated 07/03/2023, the possession of the schedule premises has been delivered to the DHR. He also made inventory that the movables of the JDR valuing of Rs.16,100/- are handed over to the DHR custody. The DHR has filed applications for attachment and sale of movables of the JDR and adjust the sale proceeds towards claim amount. In view of reasons, I.A.No.4 and 5 are allowed, the movable properties of the JDR as per the inventory of the bailiff are attached and ordered to be sold in public action. Issue sale proclamation of movables of the JDR, the spot sale is fixed by giving 07 days time from the date on which the copy of the proclamation has been affixed on the Court house, as required under Order XXI Rule 68 of CPC. Accordingly, the spot sale is on 30/03/2023. For Court sale/final bid, by 06/04/2023.

Call on 07/03/2023.

rows.Business Text: Heard the counsel for Dhr. In the instant case, Jdr.No.1 and 4 are placed exparte. Though sufficient time has been given Jdr.No.2 has not filed objection. Perused the judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has set-aside the judgment and decree passed by this court in O.S.2871/2003 and decreed the suit in favor of the plaintiffs. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has further held that judgment and decree passed in O.S.10476/1988 and in R.F.A.No.44/1996 are not binding on the plaintiffs and consequently declared the plaintiffs as the absolute owners of the suit schedule property and directed the legal representative of defendants to hand the vacant possession of the petitioin schedule property. In view of judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A. No.219/2014, I feel it is necessary to issue delivery warrant against the legal representatives of defendant/Jdrs herein. Further, as per office note, no stay or appeal pending against judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. Hence, issue delivery warrant against Jdrs to hand over the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the Dhr. R/by 22.09.2023.

hearings.judge: CCH23 XXV ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: Heard the counsel for Dhr. In the instant case, Jdr.No.1 and 4 are placed exparte. Though sufficient time has been given Jdr.No.2 has not filed objection. Perused the judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has set-aside the judgment and decree passed by this court in O.S.2871/2003 and decreed the suit in favor of the plaintiffs. The Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka has further held that judgment and decree passed in O.S.10476/1988 and in R.F.A.No.44/1996 are not binding on the plaintiffs and consequently declared the plaintiffs as the absolute owners of the suit schedule property and directed the legal representative of defendants to hand the vacant possession of the petitioin schedule property. In view of judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A. No.219/2014, I feel it is necessary to issue delivery warrant against the legal representatives of defendant/Jdrs herein. Further, as per office note, no stay or appeal pending against judgment and decree passed by the Hon\''ble High Court of Karnataka in R.F.A.No.219/2014. Hence, issue delivery warrant against Jdrs to hand over the vacant possession of the petition schedule property to the Dhr. R/by 22.09.2023.

rows.Process Title: Notice to show cause why execution should not issue [O. 21, R. 16]
rows.Hearing Judge: CCH69 LXVIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
rows.Business Text: DHR has filed this execution petition against the JDR for decreetal amount of Rs.44150 including interest from 15.01.2022 till 15.01.2023 at the rate of 12 percent p.a of Rs57395 The learned counsel for the JDR submitted that, as per the decree he has paid the entire amount and he is not liable to pay any interest. On going through the materials placed before me, this petition is filed against the judgment passed by the trial court in C.C.No.6126-2014 and judgment passed by this Court in Crl.A.No.542-2015 and order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka in Crl.R.P.No.889-2016 C/W 770-2016 before lok adalath. On going through the said order of the Hon\\\''ble High Court of Karnataka the respondent Sangana Gouda B Patil i.e the JDR herein undertook to pay the sum of Rs.8,25,000 to the present DHR and in turn the present DHR is permitted to withdraw an amount of Rs.3,83,50- deposited before the Trial Court and balance amount of Rs.4,41,500 is to be paid by the present JDR to the present DHR within 6 months from the date of the said order. On going through the order sheet the JDR has filed D.D. for Rs.2,00,000 on 21.12.2023 and again on 25.01.2024 he has handed over 2 D.Ds for an amount of Rs.1,00,000 and Rs.41,500 to the counsel for the DHR. Again on 13.03.2024 JDR filed D.D for Rs.1,00,00-. In total JDR has paid 4,41,500. hearings.judge: CCH69 LXVIII ADDL. CITY CIVIL AND SESSIONS JUDGE
hearings.business_text: DHR has filed this execution petition against the JDR for decreetal amount of Rs.44150 including interest from 15.01.2022 till 15.01.2023 at the rate of 12 percent p.a of Rs57395 The learned counsel for the JDR submitted that, as per the decree he has paid the entire amount and he is not liable to pay any interest. On going through the materials placed before me, this petition is filed against the judgment passed by the trial court in C.C.No.6126-2014 and judgment passed by this Court in Crl.A.No.542-2015 and order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka in Crl.R.P.No.889-2016 C/W 770-2016 before lok adalath. On going through the said order of the Hon\\\''ble High Court of Karnataka the respondent Sangana Gouda B Patil i.e the JDR herein undertook to pay the sum of Rs.8,25,000 to the present DHR and in turn the present DHR is permitted to withdraw an amount of Rs.3,83,50- deposited before the Trial Court and balance amount of Rs.4,41,500 is to be paid by the present JDR to the present DHR within 6 months from the date of the said order. On going through the order sheet the JDR has filed D.D. for Rs.2,00,000 on 21.12.2023 and again on 25.01.2024 he has handed over 2 D.Ds for an amount of Rs.1,00,000 and Rs.41,500 to the counsel for the DHR. Again on 13.03.2024 JDR filed D.D for Rs.1,00,00-. In total JDR has paid 4,41,500. Hence, it is clear that the JDR has already paid Rs.4,41,500 as ordered by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and this petition is filed for collecting interest at the rate of 12percent p.a, which nowhere finds place in the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka and it has not discussed regarding the interest.In the circumstances, without any speaking order DHR is not entitled to receive 12 percent interest on the principal amount. As on now, the JDR has paid the entire decreetal amount as per the order passed by the Honorable High Court of Karnataka. Hence, to report closure of execution petition by 08.08.2024.
